why: The student copies element by element (copy[i] = data2[i]), which is the right idea and is not an alias, but never creates the new array, and the loop bound i <= data2.length goes one index past the end, so the code always throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and never produces a copy.

concepts.why: The answer says nothing about int itself.
The student writes length correctly as a field with no parentheses, but uses it as if it were the last valid index.
The for header has the right form, but its bound gives the wrong number of passes.
i++ is only the standard update, and the student says nothing about it.
The student uses the element-by-element copy plan, but leaves out new int[data2.length] and runs one pass too many, so no working copy is made.
The student treats <= length as a valid bound (the OffByOneBound misconception), so the loop reaches data2[data2.length].
The answer makes no claim about primitive types.
The student uses <= where < is needed, so the loop runs length+1 times.
The student makes no statement about aliasing (there is no copy = data2).
